scenario.description: A collector who owns a vintage stereo receiver must decide whether to accept a neighbor's barter proposal or take a cash offer, then settle the exchange, handoff, equipment compatibility, and repair assurances with the people gathered at a neighborhood swap.

shared_context.S1: Elena owns a working 1970s stereo receiver that she is considering trading or selling.
shared_context.S2: Maya has brought a restored floor lamp to discuss as a possible trade item.
shared_context.S3: Jon is also interested in acquiring the receiver for cash.
shared_context.S4: The receiver powers on and produces sound through the test speakers at the swap.
shared_context.S5: Elena has been looking for a safe floor lamp for her reading room, while the receiver is surplus to her current audio setup.
shared_context.S6: At this neighborhood swap, people usually state the full terms of an offer, including the item or cash amount and when they can complete the exchange, before the owner chooses among offers.
shared_context.S7: The neighborhood swap runs from 9:00 in the morning until noon on Saturday.
shared_context.S8: Elena makes the final decision about the receiver and the terms of any deal.
shared_context.S9: Maya and Jon are both expected to state their proposed terms before Elena chooses which offer, if any, to accept.
shared_context.S10: Before Elena decides, each person who has inspected an item or tested equipment must use the swap's formal reveal procedure to state that information aloud; merely mentioning it in an ordinary comment does not complete the check-in.

PF1.text: Maya's exact proposal is to exchange the receiver for her restored floor lamp plus $40, with the handoff on Saturday at 11:00; under the swap's formal offer-disclosure step, Maya must disclose this complete binding proposal with a formal reveal action using fact_id PF1.

PF2.text: Jon will pay exactly $260 in cash for the receiver and can complete the purchase today; under the swap's formal offer-disclosure step, Jon must disclose this exact binding cash offer with a formal reveal action using fact_id PF2.

PF3.text: Ruth inspected Maya's lamp wiring for the neighborhood repair fair and found it safe; Maya will provide a 30-day repair promise for the lamp.

PF4.text: Cal tested Maya's intended speaker pair with a matching receiver and confirmed that the pair is 8-ohm compatible with Elena's receiver.

decisions.exchange_item: string; record only the core item name 'restored floor lamp', without adding the cash amount
decisions.cash_added: integer; record the separate cash component of the barter
decisions.cash_comparison: integer; record Jon's exact disclosed cash offer, not a net or adjusted amount

acceptance_conditions: Elena must accept Maya's barter proposal.
The exchange item must be recorded as the core item name 'restored floor lamp'.
Maya must add exactly $40 to the exchange.
The handoff must be set for Saturday at 11:00.
The settlement's cash_comparison must exactly record Jon's formally revealed $260 cash offer.
The lamp's wiring must be confirmed safe.
The settlement must record Maya's repair promise as exactly 30 days.
The speaker pair must be confirmed compatible with Elena's receiver.
Elena must cite Ruth's inspection when justifying the lamp safety and repair terms.

provenance_checks.P3: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and decisions['cash_comparison'] == 260

decisive_facts.why: Maya's exact formally disclosed proposal changes the accepted partner to Maya, identifies the restored floor lamp, adds exactly $40, and sets the handoff for Saturday at 11:00.
Jon's formal disclosure changes the comparison record to exactly $260 and supplies the exact revealed fact that must support that recorded amount.
Ruth's inspection changes the lamp condition from unverified to safe and establishes the exact 30-day repair promise that Elena must record and cite.
Cal's test changes the speaker compatibility decision from unverified to confirmed for the 8-ohm speaker pair used with Elena's receiver.
